source: Rast, L. 2008. 'Husbandry and Reproduction', Best Practice Health & Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia, workshop slides (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com)
text: This source sets out basic welfare needs for cattle: adequate quantity and quality of water and food, contact with other cattle (as a herd animal), enough space to stand, lie down, stretch, and turn, and protection from predators, disease, injury, and adverse or sudden weather changes, including appropriate housing. On handling, it recommends good facilities that are strong, secure, well-lit, level-floored, and free of noisy or sharp hazards, paired with handlers who have real animal-handling skill: a positive, gentle, quiet attitude, understanding of animal behaviour, ability to read the animal's actions, and patience.
